# Tic-Tac-Toe: Advisory Work Draft r2

Status: in-progress; readiness: not-assessed. Owner: ADHOC-7fd789738d5348cbbbd4f4cb378fbecf, workflow.planning. This is the current reconciliation of tic-tac-toe-work-r1, not an executable Phase, complete proposal, tracker or admission. Retain work r1 in full as history and apply the explicit revisions below to its one delivery candidate.

## Inputs

Input capture SHA-256: 8d5893679d6384baa071b3ffee1b170d1976183ade22de13a6b306c84cc9b075. Current Canon: tic-tac-toe-canon-r3, request SHA-256 b4c7fbde06e754f9451f1510ca65fa95b8d12a61672eef2e587434bcfe3d1558, including the candidates it explicitly retains from Canon r1/r2. Predecessor work request SHA-256: aeac270a616f403b36cc8263ad88a01227d05488c4bf814dbf5022e45f482ee3. The entire five-source corpus was considered, including source-5 (46d3113d1fd032c0a194c49229f11a956bf1b2de43b49f01e38df51d40417726); source-1 through source-4 retain the exact pins inventoried in Canon r3. No source is omitted or only counted. No deferred item, external diagram, product implementation or completed-work evidence has been newly selected.

## Candidate Disposition And Scope

Revise w-playable-game@r1 to w-playable-game@r2. Keep one cohesive deliverable: the playable React game served by local Node.js/Express on 3630, plus exhaustive AI/correctness tests and desktop/physical-iPhone Chrome acceptance. There is no split, new work identity or inter-candidate edge. Preserve work r1's scope/exclusions, internal prerequisites, rule/AI/library-selection guidance, timer/replay isolation tests, fixed-port checks, evidence requirements and risks except for the explicit reconciliations below.

The intended repository is this PokerNight repository at /Users/jmsimpson/Documents/GitHub/PokerNight. The earlier recommendation to isolate this feature elsewhere is superseded; do not repeat that scope objection. Inspect and follow this repository's actual product placement/toolchain conventions before assigning implementation paths. Existing unrelated work must be preserved. Repository selection alone does not choose a Git target branch or authorize commits/pushes.

## Settled Design And Interaction

Browser-held transient game state with Express serving the app is now Operator-agreed design, not an open recommendation. Integrate rule/controller/AI behavior in the browser; no server gameplay API or shared cross-device board is needed. No persistent accounts/saved games/scores are introduced. Separate browser sessions remain independent. Do not turn this into a promise of offline asset loading.

Initial mode/mark setup is followed by Start. No move, including an opening AI move, occurs before Start. Starting sets X to move; if X is AI-controlled, its first move follows the 500 ms delay. Disable mode/mark changes during an active game and permit setup changes after termination. Play again retains the displayed mode/mark and directly starts the next game, without a second Start action. Editing terminal setup values alone does not start a game. Preserve the previous board/result until an explicit new-game action. These rules reconcile the formerly open setup recommendation with r-start-setup@r1 and retained r-manual-replay@r2.

## Current Traceability

Replace every Canon-r2/story-r2 reference in work r1 with the current revision specified here; retain unchanged definitions d-human-count@r1, d-ai@r1, d-game@r1 and d-replay@r1. Current coverage is thirteen requirements and four stories:
- r-rules@r1: legal-move/outcome integration and rule tests.
- r-modes@r2: controller ownership in all three modes, shared-device operation.
- r-mark-choice@r1: X/O setup and correct opening controller.
- r-unbeatable@r1: dependency evaluation and exhaustive no-loss/legal-move proof as both marks.
- r-result@r1: turn/result rendering and terminal retention.
- r-manual-replay@r2: all-mode replay, retained selections and old-game callback isolation.
- r-react@r1: real interactive React application delivery.
- r-runtime@r1: Express/3630 startup, asset serving and occupied-port behavior.
- r-browsers@r3: actual Chrome desktop and physical-iPhone acceptance, responsive pointer/touch controls and Wi-Fi access.
- r-local-session@r1: no account flow, saved games or persistent scores.
- r-ai-pacing@r1: 500 ms scheduling, including first AI turns, without duplicate or stale moves.
- r-state-authority@r1: browser-owned transient game state, no server gameplay dependency and session independence.
- r-start-setup@r1: pre-Start inactivity, active-game setup lock and correct restart behavior.

All four stories s-solo@r3, s-watch@r3, s-two-humans@r3 and s-local-browser@r3 are realized within w-playable-game@r2; their exact requirement mappings are in Canon r3. No fabricated admitted trace IDs or legacy functionality is added. No definition meaning is changed by this work revision.

## Acceptance Updates

Retain all work-r1 tests for eight winning lines, final-cell win precedence, draw detection, legal inputs, terminal immutability, exhaustive AI-X/AI-O paths, AI/AI draw, 500 ms pacing, rapid-input handling, stale timer cancellation, manual replay, fixed port and responsive controls. Add or refine:
- For every mode, verify the board stays empty and AI timers do not produce moves before Start. Test human O and AI/AI opening moves after Start plus the required delay.
- Verify mode/mark controls cannot mutate active controller ownership, become usable after termination and do not themselves schedule a new game. Check Start/new-game and Play again behavior using the chosen visible controls and selections.
- Verify current board, controller, turn and result transitions are browser-owned, not dependent on server move APIs. Open separate browser sessions and prove they do not share a board. This is not authentication or adversarial multiplayer security.
- Run the game in actual desktop Chrome and actual Chrome on the Operator's physical iPhone over local Wi-Fi. Complete/replay games and verify touch, mode/mark setup, Start, AI observation, result retention and layout. Record exact device/OS/browser versions and tested implementation identity rather than guessing them during planning.
- Real iPhone Chrome evidence is mandatory. Desktop Chromium mobile emulation and WebKit runs may supplement testing but are not a substitute for the named physical browser. Do not infer identical rendering engines or behavior from the Chrome brand on desktop and iPhone.

## Browser Matrix Reconciliation

Required families: Chrome desktop and Chrome iPhone only, as selected by the Operator. The wider Firefox/Safari/Android gate proposed in work r1 is withdrawn from required acceptance; optional checks must not be represented as an additional Operator requirement or as proof of those products' support.

For automated layout checks, retain 1280x800 desktop and 390x844 mobile with a 320px-width stress check as proposed engineering test dimensions, not claimed dimensions of the Operator's devices. Physical acceptance uses and records the real viewport. Implementation may adjust representative automated dimensions with rationale while still satisfying the responsive requirement. Actual version/device recording is evidence collection, not a renewed scope decision.

## Dependencies And Verification Plan

Keep work r1's internal prerequisite structure: inspect actual implementation context and choose suitable verified dependencies; integrate rules/AI; build UI/controllers/timers/setup/replay; deliver Express serving; verify the combined application. Express setup can proceed alongside rules/UI; integrated browser acceptance needs both. New pre-Start/state-authority checks belong to the same candidate rather than artificial new phases.

The advisory graph is one node with no inter-candidate edges and is acyclic. No repository execution DAG is created or modified, and no external Phase dependencies are invented. Actual baseline compatibility must be checked before complete proposal construction. These planning checks do not prove any game implementation or test result.

## Risk And Review Implications

Retain exhaustive AI verification and stale-schedule controls. Agreed Start prevents AI play before setup completion; locked active settings prevent mid-turn ownership changes. iPhone Chrome testing addresses platform behavior that desktop emulation cannot establish. Deliberate LAN serving must preserve the local-use scope without public exposure; implementation documents the selected bind/access setup and requires authority for any host/firewall mutation. No server is launched here.

The three substantive work-r1 questions about design, physical browser targets and repository destination are resolved by source-5. Their old text remains historical, not current blockers. Remaining work is operational setup and contract completion: choose the target branch, obtain the exact committed operational specification/execution baseline, inspect destination conventions and finalize the proposed executable contract. None is fabricated or initialized by this pass.

No independent review/approval exists to carry onto this revised subject. No historical nonconformance or completed-phase rework is claimed. The architecture/pre-flight diagram obligation recorded in work r1 remains for any later complete phase prompt adopting these boundaries; no phase prompt or diagram is created in this advisory operation. There is no schema expansion.

## Next Boundary

The next planning boundary is explicitly requested complete-proposal preparation once the exact target/baseline and required contract inputs are available. Repository initialization, commits, formal review/approval, publication, merge/application verification and product start remain separate authorized operations. Do not treat 'land it in this repo' as having already performed them. Terminal condition remains in-progress; readiness not-assessed.
questions: Select the Git target branch and provide the exact committed operational specification/execution baseline before constructing a complete proposal; this repository is already selected.
